parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a federal document and entry regime that treats any sex-marker discrepancy as grounds for refusal or lifetime fraud ineligibility (trans travelers report passports blocked, foreign advisories issued) with a division that operatively criminalises gender expression (upheld drag/impersonation ban, felony on repeat), mandates birth-sex facility use, and treats gender-congruent restroom use as indecent exposure. A documented 2025 arrest ended with 24 hours in a men's ward — tier 1/2 state-imposed exposure with no statewide discrimination remedy. Gender-affirming care for minors is banned, penalising adults who assist a travelling trans minor. Custody placement by birth-sex is statutory. The 7.8/100k killing figure is an undercount floor and carries no evidentiary weight; dated police-indifference reports and the available panic defence are secondary. Custody assault frequency and drag-ban application to everyday presentation are unresolved. Imprisonment is possible but not highly likely; execution is not credible — placing this below the 0.35 exclusion-only anchors and above the 0.15 custody-violence tier.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order ends X markers and self-selected gender on passports/visas; Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and allows lifetime fraud ineligibility consideration; trans travelers report passports confiscated or blocked, some stranded abroad; eight foreign governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Findings require all four fraud elements, are never automatic, and limited waivers exist; existing X-marker passports remain valid to expiry; litigation is pending and several orders are enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: A document/presentation mismatch can escalate from secondary screening to refused entry or fraud allegation, then into detention where birth-sex placement rules apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented March 2025 arrest of a trans woman in a capitol restroom (trespass, up to 60 days), held 24 hours in the men's ward; 2026 statute mandates birth-sex prison placement; 2019 statute defines gender-congruent restroom use as indecent exposure; federal custody shows conversion-therapy-style policies, beatings and sexual abuse for transgender immigration detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; one 2019 state opinion allows gender-based sentencing enhancement.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility exclusion plus a birth-sex custody rule means an arrest on a facilities charge routes the traveller directly into cross-sex housing — the documented 2025 case shows the chain operating.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law requires facilities matching sex assigned at birth, bars trans women from women's shelters, and criminalises some gender-expressive performance publicly (misdemeanour first offence, 1–6 year felony on repeat — upheld, cert denied Feb 2025); nationwide, facility bans cover all government buildings in 10 units, with criminal triggers in 4.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Sign-post mandate struck down (2022); one school bathroom ban remains in litigation; 29 units plus the capital have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor entering a public building, shelter, or performing visibly can trigger both the facilities regime and the criminal expression statute in the same outing.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors (upheld June 2025), extends to out-of-state telehealth, penalises adults who help a minor obtain it ($25,000 provider actions), and bans care for inmates; national Oct 2025 rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for trans under-18s; federal subpoenaed 'over 20' hospitals for under-19 patient records.
care_services.protection: Emergency care is not documented as denied; several federal orders are enjoined or unresolved.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor risks provider refusal, civil liability for the guardian, and state inquiry — separation of care from the travelling child.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State law defines sex by anatomy/genetics at birth; national rhetoric frames gender-affirming care as 'mutilation' and directs law enforcement to investigate 'gender ideology'; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; state ranks in the worst tier for laws passed and lowest for LGBTQ rights; hate-crime statute omits gender identity; gay/trans panic defence remains available.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism text says powers will not target mere disagreement; reward criteria do not list gender ideology; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment protection exists federally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing shapes how charges and investigations against an outed visitor are pursued, and discounts the value of paper federal protections.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care felony/civil-penalty regime for adults assisting a minor's transition; mandated parental outing of name/pronoun requests in schools; sports and bathroom restrictions by birth sex; adoption agencies may refuse LGBTQ parents; guardian accompanying a trans minor carries the adult's liability.
minors_guardians.protection: School-enforcement directive enjoined July 2022; sports litigation partially decided and ongoing; several federal orders blocked.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family crossing into custody or school settings can convert a care question into an investigation of the guardian.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Gay/trans panic defence usable to mitigate fatal attacks; 2021 reporting of officials turning a blind eye to LGBTQ assaults; documented discrimination, service refusal and beatings; no statewide non-discrimination law; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2019 state opinion allows gender-based sentencing enhancement; several municipal public-employment ordinances.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of statewide coverage means an assaulted visitor depends on federal charging discretion and unenthusiastic local response.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Suits over licence markers, school bathroom law, drag-ban follow-on litigation and passport rules are unresolved; enforcement of the 2026 facility/shelter Act and 2024 prison care ban is unsourced; indecent-exposure enforcement frequency against trans people unknown; state has no statewide discrimination remedy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, a running legal-aid FAQ on document rules, national employment precedent, and several successfully enjoined federal orders show functioning but partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Pending litigation means exposure shifts with the moment of travel, and local remedies are pre-empted or absent for public accommodations.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than ours: Varnalia routes document mismatch into routine arrest, months in pretrial custody with guard beatings and an available capital clause. Here custody abuse is documented mainly at the federal immigration level, arrest is rare (one known facilities arrest), and no credible execution pathway exists — so well above 0.15.

Closest fit: birth-sex prison placement with frequent assaults, a criminalised cross-dressing statute, arrests, brief sentences, no execution, slow remedies. Ours shares birth-sex custody and an operative expression statute but lacks documented frequency of custody assault or raids; the federal document regime adds a universal entry exposure 0.25-C lacks. Slightly above, same tier region.

Vellandra's register excludes and humiliates but explicitly produces no arrest or charge. Our jurisdiction documents an actual arrest with cross-sex ward detention, an upheld criminal impersonation statute with felony escalation, and an indecent-exposure theory — all state-imposed with no statewide remedy. Worse than 0.35, hence 0.30.

Far above ours: recognised nonbinary passports, trained officers, released detainees' apologies, no criminalisation of gender expression, structural remedies operating. Every one of those features is inverted or absent here — markers are closed, expression is criminal, remedies are pending — confirming the large gap below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one continuous federal exposure (closed markers, discrepancy-driven refusal, fraud-ineligibility exposure, documented strandings and foreign advisories) layered over a division that independently criminalises gender expression and mandates birth-sex facilities, shelters and prison placement. These interact: a document mismatch at entry can become an investigation, an arrest on a facilities or expression charge routes into cross-sex custody, and the state has no discrimination remedy to interrupt the chain. A guardian travelling with a trans minor adds a care-liability layer with provider refusal and possible state inquiry. Paper protections — federal employment precedent, national hate-crime coverage, pending litigation — are real but partial and pre-empted locally. The violence figure is an undercount floor and unusable; dated indifference reports and the panic defence colour severity without establishing rate. Worst documented feature sits in tier 1 with a documented tier-2 arrest, above the 0.35 exclusion-only anchors, below working-remedy tiers.
